title_en: This Lord of the Rings Headset Stand Can Charge Your PS5 Controller With the Power of Sauron and the One Ring
body_en:
There are a lot of good Lord of the Rings gifts out there, but there are surprisingly few options for gamers specifically. Sure, you can buy any of the many LOTR games , but what if you just want a nice accessory to showcase your love for Tolkien's work? Well now there's a gaming headset and PS5 controller charger combo that will let you do just that.
Grupo Erik, who has created a variety of officially licensed LOTR products, currently has a version of Sauron's hand that will hold your headset and charge your PS5 controller for you. And the best part? It's actually really affordable right now.
The Sauron's hand charger is currently only $54.90 at Amazon, which is relatively cheap for an officially licensed product. The hand itself can hold most wireless gaming headsets and the charger is compatible with PS5 DualSense controllers . All you need to do is plug it in, dock your controller in the designated spot, and let the magic happen. And by magic I mean the fact that the One Ring will actually glow while your controller charges.
As far as PS5 controller chargers go, it's a bit more expensive than some of the options available on Amazon. You can find a charging dock that is compatible with multiple controllers at once for around $20 if you do a bit of shopping. That being said, a standard PS5 charger isn't going to have nearly the same aura as Sauron's hand. The details on this thing are what make it great, and the added benefit of the inscription on the One Ring actually glowing is just the cherry on top.
If you like this PS5 accessory, it's worth pointing out that Grupo Erik also makes the overall best LOTR bookends on the market right now. The Pillars of Kings make for the perfect addition to any physical media collection and we definitely recommend checking them out.
Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, he has considered the Northwest his home for his entire life. With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics — from TV series to books and the latest LEGO sets .
